text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + timeouts for tenant 'tenant-phoenix' on Dedicated cluster eu-west-1-dc2. 5xx spiked from 0.5% -> 12% in last 3m. Link: https://mon.redwood/alerts/1767001234 :rotating_light:

Jordan (oncall): I'm on it. Paging SRE: @Lee, can you join?

Lee (sre): on call, joining. Pulling dashboards now.

Ana (eng-runtime): FYI I see CPU steady but GPU mem pressure high on nodes gpu-03,gpu-04. Latency tail up too.

Maya (cs): Customer support has a few tickets from Phoenix about timeouts around 12:10 UTC. They report ~30% failed responses.

Jordan (oncall): Can someone run `kubectl get pods -n dedicated-tenant-phoenix -o wide` and dump pod logs for the last 2m?

Lee (sre): Running:
```
kubectl get pods -n dedicated-tenant-phoenix
NAME                                 READY STATUS   RESTARTS   AGE
inference-0                          1/1   Running   0          5d
inference-1                          0/1   CrashLoop  4          2h
inference-2                          1/1   Running   0          3d
```
Logs show repeated OOM/kernel kills on inference-1 and long GC stalls.

Ana (eng-runtime): paste of pod logs:
```
[2026-03-14T12:09:57Z] OOMKilled: qkv_cache exceeded 9800MB
[2026-03-14T12:10:01Z] WARNING: failed to allocate KV cache shard
[2026-03-14T12:10:04Z] 504 gateway timeout upstream
```
Looks like a single replica is getting large requests, eating the GPU memory and triggering evictions.

Lee (sre): Node metrics:
- gpu-03 memory used 99% (two tenants sharing)
- node evictions on gpu-03 at 12:08-12:11
I suspect noisy tenant within same node (not phoenix?) that spiked and pushed phoenix pod to OOM. Need to confirm process owner.

Jordan (oncall): @Ana can you check which containers on gpu-03 are hot? `nvidia-smi pmon -c` and `crictl stats` should show.

Ana (eng-runtime): Running quick checks:
```
PID   GPU_MEM  CMD
4231  10240    /usr/bin/serve --model gpt-large
7890  12288    /usr/bin/serve --model gpt-xxl  <-- big
```
PID 7890 belongs to tenant-id: t-997 (different tenant). That's the noisy process.

Lee (sre): Confirmed. t-997 is colocated on gpu-03 and is using sustained >12GB. That pushed available memory below threshold and caused phoenix pod's allocator to fail.

Maya (cs): Customer-facing note: Phoenix reports "intermittent timeouts and errors". I'm composing an update: "We are investigating elevated errors and short-term mitigations in progress. Next update in 20m."

Jordan (oncall): Mitigation options:
1) Evict noisy tenant container (force kill) on gpu-03.
2) Temporarily throttle tenant t-997 via rate-limit at the gateway.
3) Drain/cordon gpu-03 and migrate phoenix to another node (risky, takes time).
4) Provision quick extra capacity in eu-west-1-dc2 (if available) and shift phoenix.
Which one do we take now?

Lee (sre): Fastest is to throttle or kill noisy PID. Throttle at gateway to avoid collateral. I'll push a temporary rate-limit rule for t-997 to 20r/s.

ops-bot: Applied rate-limit policy: `tenant:t-997 -> 20 r/s` (rule id rl-5532).

Ana (eng-runtime): After throttling, I'm seeing GPU mem drop on gpu-03 to 65% over next 40s. phoenix pod memory recover and inference-1 restarted successfully. Errors drop to ~1.8%.

Jordan (oncall): Great. Maya please send the customer update: "We applied traffic controls to reduce error rates; errors are declining. We'll follow up with root cause and mitigation plan."

Maya (cs): Sent update to Phoenix. They replied: thanks, keep us posted.

Lee (sre): Temporary mitigation effective. But root cause: tenant colocated workload t-997 started large-batch generation (long contexts) causing sustained KV cache allocations. Our colocated scheduling allowed >1 heavy tenant per GPU in this pool. We need a durable fix.

Ana (eng-runtime): Proposed next steps:
- Add automatic memory-aware placement: avoid colocating two high-mem tenants on same GPU.
- Enforce per-tenant GPU memory cap via cgroup/allocator.
- Add early soft-TTL for KV caches on memory pressure.
- Emergency: enable tenant pinning so phoenix can move to spare nodes when pressure detected.

Jordan (oncall): Filing incident postmortem. Short postmortem template: impact, timeline, root cause, mitigation, customer impact, action items. I'll assign follow-ups.

Lee (sre): Action items (short-term):
- (P0) Add gateway tenant rate-limit option to Dedicated console (ENG/Runtime & Platform) - owner: Ana - due EOD.
- (P1) Implement memory-aware placement for scheduler - owner: Lee - due next sprint.
- (P1) Document emergency ops playbook for evicting noisy tenants - owner: Jordan - due 48h.

Ana (eng-runtime): I'll open PR for the rate-limit UI config and a runtime guard to enforce GPU mem caps.

Jordan (oncall): Final status: incident mitigated, error rate back down to baseline ~0.6%. Customer notified, CS tracking. Transitioning to post-incident follow-up. Closing thread for live paging.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring, severity lowered. Incident ticket linked: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0314-01

Maya (cs): Adding customer impact summary to ticket: "Tenant Phoenix experienced elevated 5xx/timeouts for ~9 minutes starting 12:08 UTC. Estimated 30% of in-flight requests failed; we applied throttling to a noisy colocated tenant which restored service. No data lost. Next steps: schedule capacity isolation and placement fixes."

Jordan (oncall): Thanks all. We'll run a short retro at 16:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
